summary: Ran the configured check (passes) and a repro script in scratch. The tests are too weak to catch any of the defects below. Assumed percentile semantics are not specified, so only the range/error behaviour and the even-length median are judged against the stated intent and REVIEW.md.

findings.title: percentile(xs, 100) raises IndexError although p=100 must be accepted
findings.evidence: k = int(len(s) * p / 100) gives k == len(s) for p=100, so s[k] is out of range. Repro: percentile([1,2,3,4], 100) -> IndexError: list index out of range. The stated requirement is that p accepts [0, 100] inclusive.
findings.suggestion: Clamp the index only for the valid p==100 case (e.g. k = min(int(len(s)*p/100), len(s)-1)), or use an interpolation formula. Add a test for p=0 and p=100.

findings.title: Out-of-range p is not rejected with ValueError; negative p silently wraps to a wrong value
findings.evidence: REVIEW.md: 'Never silently clamp invalid input; raise ValueError.' Repro: percentile([1,2,3,4], -1) -> 1 and percentile([1,2,3,4], -50) -> 3 (negative list indexing returns an arbitrary element, no error). percentile(..., 150) -> IndexError rather than ValueError. NaN gives a ValueError from int() only by accident; bool True is accepted as 1.
findings.suggestion: Validate at the top: if not (0 <= p <= 100): raise ValueError('p must be in [0, 100]') (this also rejects NaN, since the comparison is False). Add tests with pytest.raises(ValueError) for -1, 100.1, nan.

findings.title: median() returns the upper-middle element for even-length input
findings.evidence: mid = len(s)//2; return s[mid]. Repro: median([1,2,3,4]) -> 3, but the median is 2.5. The test only covers an odd-length list so it does not detect this.
findings.suggestion: For even length return (s[mid-1] + s[mid]) / 2. Add an even-length test.

findings.title: Empty input is not handled; median([]) and percentile([], p) raise raw IndexError, and docstrings do not state error behaviour
findings.evidence: REVIEW.md: 'Every public function must have a docstring that states its error behaviour.' median docstring is 'Return the median of a list of numbers.' and percentile docstring is just 'p in [0, 100].'; neither mentions any exceptions. Repro: median([]) and percentile([], 50) -> IndexError: list index out of range.
findings.suggestion: Raise ValueError('empty input') explicitly for empty xs and document 'Raises ValueError if xs is empty (or p outside [0, 100])' in both docstrings.

findings.title: Tests do not cover boundaries, error paths or even-length median
findings.evidence: Only test_median([3,1,2]) and test_percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) were added. No test for p=0, p=100 (the required inclusive range), invalid p, empty input, or an even-length median, so the check passes while p=100 crashes and even median is wrong. The percentile semantic (nearest-rank variant giving 3 for p=50 on [1,2,3,4]) is also undocumented and pinned only by that single assertion.
findings.suggestion: Add tests for p=0, p=100, p out of range / NaN raising ValueError, empty list raising ValueError, and median of an even-length list; document the percentile method in the docstring.
